newsitem.title: CANADA: Petro-Canada reports record results for '96.
newsitem.headline: Petro-Canada reports record results for '96.

text.p: Petro-Canada on Thursday reported record financial results for 1996, bolstered by strong oil and natural gas prices and growing production volumes.

Petro-Canada, Canada's largest independent integrated energy firm, said net earnings for the year were C$247 million or C$0.94 per share, an jump from C$196 million or C$0.79 per share the year before.
Revenues totalled C$5.6 billion up from C$4.8 billion in 1995.
Fourth-quarter earnings rose to C$101 million or C$0.38 per share, up sharply from C$65 million or C$0.76 per share in the same period the year before.
The formerly government-controlled company said fourth-quarter earnings in its upstream oil and gas production division totalled C$94 million, up from C$41 million in same quarter of 1995.
The improvement reflected higher output and prices for crude oil, natural gas liquids and natural gas, it said.
The upstream division's performance, however, was partially offset by increased depreciation, depletion and amortization charges and hedging costs.
Petro-Canada said its downstream refining and marketing unit earned C$30 million from operations during the fourth quarter, down C$11 million from the previous year.
Rising feedstock costs continued to squeeze profit margins during the period but some ground was made up from higher refined product sales, Petro-Canada said.
